predictions.experiment: MATH-500: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base hit the cap and was wrong
predictions.recipe: Read studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; select problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == true. Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl (code_cue); join on problem_index (if an index has several rows, use the first in file order; a missing row counts as wrong). Statistic: number of selected problems with score_v3 == 1 in 0203, divided by the number of selected problems.
predictions.note: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (t1_right is grader v3, t1_cap_hit) and iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl (code_cue, run_cell row with score_v3, cap_hit), fetched to runs/theory-tests/r4m09/<job>/. Select t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit is True; first 0203 row per problem_index; missing row = wrong, kept in the denominator. Alt reading: missing 0203 rows dropped from the denominator (same as main if 0203 has all 500). score_v3 == 1 means correct. An empty selection prints not_computable, because the recipe does not say how to count it. Possible error sources: per_problem T1 comes from S3 T1.jsonl regraded with v3, while 0203 uses its stored score_v3 column. The two should be the same grader version, but this was not checked. The selected group is small (the base's MATH-500 cap-hit-and-wrong set), so the fraction is noisy.

predictions.experiment: MATH-500: Code-RL cue fix rate minus random-difference cue fix rate on base clean-finished-wrong problems
predictions.recipe: Read studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json; select problems with t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit == false (set W). Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl (code_cue) and iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl (random_cue); join each on problem_index (first row in file order per index; a missing row counts as wrong). Statistic: (count of W with score_v3 == 1 in 0203 minus count of W with score_v3 == 1 in 6429) divided by |W|.
predictions.note: Files: per_problem.json (W = t1_right == 0 and t1_cap_hit is False), 0203 (code_cue) and iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-153047-6429/answers.jsonl (random_cue). First row per problem_index in each; missing = wrong. Statistic: (code correct in W - random correct in W) / |W|; refuted if > 0.12. Alt reading: W restricted to problems present in both files. Note: the random_cue cell is base + a random Gaussian difference, not a fresh base sample. The recipe uses it as the 'fresh sample' control as written. Some W problems carry a hand label and may include unparsable-answer endings (finished, not capped, but graded wrong for format), which an ending policy could fix. The recipe does not exclude these, so they could inflate the Code number in a way that cuts against the theory.

predictions.experiment: MATH-500: cap-hit rate of Code-RL cue answers
predictions.recipe: Fetch iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-162452-0203/answers.jsonl; keep the first row per problem_index (500 problems). Statistic: number of rows with cap_hit == true divided by 500 (a missing problem counts as not a cap hit but stays in the denominator).
predictions.note: File: 0203. First row per problem_index, restricted to indices 0-499. cap_hit is True counted, divided by 500 (missing = no cap hit, stays in the denominator); refuted if > 0.026. Alt reading: divided by the number of distinct problems present. cap_hit is the generator's flag (n_new reached max_tokens); finish_reason was not used.

predictions.experiment: hard328: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base hit the cap and was wrong
predictions.recipe: Fetch s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_wdiff328-01/abaybektursun-1114-181216-a619/answers.jsonl (Code-RL cue). First row per problem_index in each. Select problems where e72c has cap_hit == true and score_v3 == 0. Statistic: number of selected problems with a619 score_v3 == 1 divided by the number selected; a problem missing from a619 counts as wrong; problems missing from e72c are excluded.
predictions.note: Files: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r5/day1_hard328-01/abaybektursun-1114-151534-e72c/answers.jsonl (base cue) and .../day1_wdiff328-01/abaybektursun-1114-181216-a619/answers.jsonl (Code-RL cue), fetched with --profile iterate-ecr. First row per problem_index. Select e72c cap_hit is True and score_v3 == 0; problems missing from e72c are excluded automatically, since the selection iterates over e72c. A619 missing = wrong. Refuted if < 0.19. Alt reading: a619-missing problems dropped from the denominator. A cap-hit base answer that still scored 1 is not selected, as written. Empty selection prints not_computable.

predictions.experiment: hard328: Code-RL cue accuracy on problems where the cued base finished without a cap hit and was wrong
predictions.recipe: Same two files and first-row rule as the previous recipe (e72c base cue, a619 Code-RL cue). Select problems where e72c has cap_hit == false and score_v3 == 0. Statistic: number of selected problems with a619 score_v3 == 1 divided by the number selected; a problem missing from a619 counts as wrong; problems missing from e72c are excluded.
predictions.note: Same files and rules as k=4, but select e72c cap_hit is False and score_v3 == 0. Refuted if > 0.26. Alt reading: a619-missing problems dropped from the denominator. As in k=2, 'finished but wrong' includes answers whose final line did not parse under grader v3 (format failures), which an ending policy could repair. The recipe does not separate them, which may push the number up against the theory. Different seeds (3,000,000+i base vs 71,000,000+i Code) and a different tokenizer (RL tokenizer for Code) are part of the arms as stored.
